evidence.description: The extraction manifest records exactly four archive members: datasheet, Stata source, SAS source and Identifiers.txt.
The datasheet documents historical receipt of the DOJ FOIA-derived event data, PACER review, defendant matching and manual GVKEY checks.
evidence.quote:
Data on whistleblower events was obtained from Professor David F. Engstrom (Professor of Law
at Stanford University) via Email on July 23, 2015. Engstrom obtained the data through a series
of requests to the DOJ under the Freedom of Information Act (see Engstrom [2013] for details).
His data included the following case information: the date the lawsuit was received by the court,
the court docket number of the lawsuit, the caption of the lawsuit, the judicial district where the
lawsuit was filed, the primary agency alleged of being defrauded, the DOJ’s election decision and
election date, and the settlement date as well as amounts. We then download the court filing for
each lawsuit from the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system. We manually
review the court docket filing associated with each case and match the name of every publicly
listed defendant to a GVKEY identifier. Specifically, we first apply a fuzzy-match approach to
match the names of the defendant firms to Compustat company names. We then manually review
this matching procedure and only keep correctly identified pairs. The paper describes how the final

evidence.description: The datasheet documents the February 2017 USAspending acquisition and parent-company name matching with manual review.
evidence.quote:
We obtain information on government contracts from the USAspending.gov website maintained
by the Department of Treasury’s Bureau of Fiscal Services. We downloaded the data in February
2017. The database does not contain common identifiers such as GVKEY or PERMNO, so we use
a machine-learning program to fuzzy-match over 596,000 parent company names to the names of
our whistleblower companies, then hand-check identified pairs to ensure correct matching.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes FEC PAC matching, CRP lobbying matching and the author-defined board-connection indicator.
evidence.quote:
Political Connections
We obtain data on firms’ Political Action Committee (PAC) contributions from the Federal
Election Commission’s (FEC) website. As this database does not contain common identifiers such
as GVKEY or PERMNO, we again fuzzy match the names of the PACs to the names of our
whistleblower companies. Finally, we hand-check identified pairs to ensure correct matching.
We obtain data on firms’ lobbying expenditures from the Center for Responsive Politics (CRP).
Again, we fuzzy match the company names of the CRP database to the names of our whistleblower
companies. Finally, we hand-check identified pairs to ensure correct matching.
We obtain data on political connections of firms’ board members from firms’ Def14a filings. If (at
least) one of a firm’s board members has been president, (vice-)presidential candidate, senator,

congressman, governor, mayor, chairman of the Party Caucus, member of the president’s cabinet,
White House staff, or campaign staff, we define the board as politically connected.

evidence.description: The datasheet says the supplied programs use SAS and Stata, with primary analyses in Stata.

The steps necessary to process the data used in the final analyses are described in the Data Section

Further detail of the steps taken to collect the data and the corresponding code can be found in the

dependency_review.description: Seventeen distinct annual USAspending input files are one required product family; each year has the same unresolved product, field, DUNS and history contract.
Each v2 annual table is produced from its same-year raw contract input by the supplied parent-DUNS normalization.
The supplied code reads the author-prepared DUNS-to-GVKEY crosswalk for all annual contract joins.
The 17 annual GVKEY join tables are generated by left-joining the annual v2 contracts to all_contracts.
The 17 annual gvkey2 tables are generated by the same nonmissing-GVKEY filter.
contracts_gvkey is generated by appending the filtered annual tables.
cases_wb is a separately required prepared event/case input joined by GVKEY.
The violation-filter and contract aggregation tables are produced from the combined contracts and cases using the supplied event and contract transformations.
yq_codes is read as the quarter-index lookup; it has no producer in the supplied SAS source.
funda is the annual Compustat input for the fiscal-year-end lookup.
fyend is produced from the annual Compustat input with GVKEY and fiscal-year-end fields.
contracts_aggregated_2 is generated by joining the initial contract aggregates to yq_codes and fyend.
fundq is the quarterly Compustat input for the event panel.
compustat_q2, basic_wb and compustat_q_merge are generated from fundq and cases_wb by the supplied steps.
The supplied code generates panel1 through panel4 with contract/Compustat joins and quarter-event windows.
yq_codes_e and panel5 are generated from yq_codes and the election-event quarter mappings.
def_agencies is generated from the agency codes in cases_wb.
panel6 is produced by joining the generated agency mapping to panel5.
political_connections2 is a required prepared firm-year PAC/lobby input; the govt libref is handled as a separate configuration issue.
political, political2 and panel7 are generated from the prepared political table and existing panel/case inputs.
Board is a separate prepared firm-year political-connection indicator input.
panel8 is produced by the supplied board merge and subsequent variable construction; the SIC input contract remains a separate requirement.
The contractor-rank macro reads and rewrites its generated annual contracts_minimal and contract_by_co tables.
The 17 contract_by_co_2000–2016 annual outputs are produced by the contractor-ranking macro.
largest_contractors is assembled and sorted from the 17 annual contractor-rank outputs.
The DoD contractor-rank macro generates and rereads annual contractdod_by_co tables.
The 17 contractdod_by_co_2000–2016 annual outputs are produced by the DoD contractor-ranking macro.
largestdod_contractors and largest_contractors_all_dod are generated by appending and joining the two rank branches.
link_table_complete is a distinct read input joined by parentdunsnumber in the contractor branch.
compustat_sic is the supplied-name SIC input required for the panel8 join; candidate Compustat tables do not yet verify its author mapping.
sic is generated from compustat_sic by normalizing the GVKEY and SIC fields.
The Stata input file is read, but the supplied SAS program has no final export producer; this edge remains an unresolved handoff issue.
